title: Do Dental Implants Hurt? Pain, Recovery & Timeline 2026
seoTitle: Do Dental Implants Hurt? Pain and Recovery Timeline
seoDescription: Most implant patients feel short-term soreness that peaks within 48 hours and eases with simple care. See the day-by-day timeline from our Valencia team.
excerpt: What implant surgery really feels like: a day-by-day recovery timeline, pain-control options, warning signs, and how it compares with extractions.
keyTakeaways: Most patients report mild to moderate pain that peaks in the first 24 to 48 hours and drops to mild by day 3.
Swelling usually peaks at 48 to 72 hours; ice first, switch to warm compresses after 48 hours, and sleep with your head raised.
NSAIDs such as ibuprofen are first-line; opioids are reserved for extensive cases and used in limited amounts.
Osseointegration takes 3 to 6 months, but most daily activities resume within 3 to 7 days.
Call your dentist if pain increases after 72 hours, or if you have fever, drainage, or lasting numbness.
